IMULink streams raw IMU sensor data from your Android phone to any computer on the same Wi-Fi network using UDP. You can record or process the data in Python, MATLAB, C#, or any language that supports UDP sockets.
Connect your phone and computer to the same Wi-Fi network.
Open Settings and enter your computer\'s IP address and UDP port.
Run the receiver script on your computer (see UDP Format below).
Press START STREAMING on the home screen.
Data will arrive at your computer at the configured sample rate.
macOS / Linux: open Terminal and type ifconfig — look for inet.
Windows: open Command Prompt and type ipconfig — look for IPv4 Address.
Your phone\'s own IP is shown at the bottom of the home screen.
Free tier: streaming stops after 5 minutes. Sample rate capped at 50 Hz.
Pro (one-time purchase): unlimited streaming time and full sensor rate.
Use a 5 GHz Wi-Fi network for lowest latency.
Keep the phone plugged in during long recording sessions.
The ⚡ button engages top-speed mode (Pro only).
If packets are dropped, lower the sample rate in Settings.
Settings cannot be changed while streaming is active.

IMULink uses the Android sensor coordinate system. With the phone face-up on a flat surface: X points toward the right edge, Y points toward the top edge, Z points upward away from the screen. All angular measurements follow the right-hand rule.

Every UDP datagram is a single UTF-8 encoded CSV line followed by a newline character. Fields are always in the order shown below. If a sensor is disabled in Settings, its fields are omitted entirely — there are no placeholder zeros. The timestamp is always present as the first field.

You can share this entire Help & Guide page directly with an AI assistant such as Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini to generate a complete custom receiver application. The AI will understand the UDP packet format, field names, units, and coordinate system and can write a full GUI application in Python, MATLAB, C#, Unity, or any other language you need. IMULink is open source. The full Android source code is available on GitHub. You are welcome to fork, modify, and redistribute under the project licence.
